intro: Compliance managers coordinate teams, persuade leaders and judge risk, skills used across business and government. The closest of the 25 careers below is Compliance Officers, with a 92% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $80,730, and every option needs no more education than you have.
why_it_works: Your work is turning complex rules into practical steps and convincing busy people to follow them. O*NET rates coordination at 3.75 out of 5 for this job and persuasion at 3.62. Management analysis, HR, benefits and security management use the same skills every day. BLS reports compliance managers within a broader group, so this page lists medians rather than percent changes.
tips: Management Analysts earn $101,860 and are a 90% match; consulting firms value compliance experience.
Human Resources Managers earn $149,280 and are an 82% match.
Lead a cross-team project to build experience managing people, one of your main gaps.

faq.q: What jobs can former compliance managers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Compliance Officers (92%), Management Analysts (90%) and regulatory affairs specialists (89%), based on O*NET 31.0. Compensation and benefits specialists are also 87% matched, with a median of $78,210, and work closely with employment rules.

faq.q: Which jobs for compliance managers pay the most?
faq.a: Among the 25 matches, the highest medians are Financial Managers at $166,570, Human Resources Managers at $149,280 and Compensation and Benefits Managers at $149,230, according to BLS May 2025 data. All three are 80% or more similar to compliance management.

faq.q: Do compliance managers need another degree?
faq.a: No. All 25 matches usually need no more education than compliance managers already have, including all of the top 10. A bachelor's degree is the norm, held by 57% of workers in a close match, so your experience with audits and policies matters more than new schooling.

faq.q: What skills should compliance managers build?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are complex problem solving, managing people, operations analysis and service orientation. Judgment and social perceptiveness already rate 3.5 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so leading teams is the main step toward senior management.
